summary: The Medicare Advantage Improvement Act of 2026 makes several changes to the Medicare Advantage program regarding prior authorizations, timeframes for decision-making, claims processing, medical necessity criteria, plan oversight, and network adequacy.

affected_groups.effect: Enrollees will experience faster decision timeframes for prior authorizations, reduced administrative hurdles for clinical adjustments during treatment, and ensured alignment of medical necessity and network standards with original fee-for-service Medicare.

Plans must implement real-time authorization systems, meet tighter response deadlines, adhere to standardized medical necessity criteria, report detailed data, and face potential compliance scoring, tier-based payment reductions, and star rating adjustments.

Providers benefit from real-time automated approvals for routine items and services, prompt payment requirements for all clean claims, and restrictions on retrospective claim denials and coding changes by plans.

key_provisions: Reduces timeframes for Medicare Advantage organizations to respond to standard and expedited prior authorization and concurrent determination requests to 72 hours and 24 hours respectively, starting January 1, 2028.

Requires Medicare Advantage plans to have automated real-time authorization processes for certain high-approval, low-risk, or high-burden items and services submitted through certified electronic health record technology beginning January 1, 2028.
Prohibits Medicare Advantage plans from requiring new authorizations for clinical modifications, extensions, or adjustments made while an approved item or service is being furnished.

Establishes a compliance scoring and accountability program for Medicare Advantage organizations, applying payment reductions ranging from 1.0 to 2.0 percent for organizations in lower compliance tiers, and adds a compliance domain to the Star Ratings system.

Restricts Medicare Advantage organizations from applying medical necessity criteria that are more restrictive than original Medicare fee-for-service standards and codifies the two-midnight inpatient admission benchmark.

Applies prompt payment requirements and automated review and payment processes to both in-network and out-of-network claims, and restricts retroactive denials, code changes, and clawbacks for authorized services.
Modifies network adequacy standards to require that Medicare Advantage plans provide adequate access to long-term care hospitals and inpatient rehabilitation facilities starting January 1, 2028.
missing_information: Specific dollar amounts or baseline budgetary costs for implementing the compliance scoring and real-time processing systems.
Exact definitions and numerical thresholds that the Secretary of Health and Human Services will establish through future rulemaking for low-risk services, compliance scores, and penalty tiers.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Medicare Advantage Improvement Act of 2026 makes several changes to the Medicare Advantage program regarding prior authorizations, timeframes for decision-making, claims processing, medical necessity criteria, plan oversight, and network adequacy.
summary_detail.significance: This bill introduces sweeping changes to how Medicare Advantage plans manage prior authorizations, process claims, and ensure compliance. It directly alters timelines, payment rules, and oversight mechanisms across the entire Medicare Advantage program starting in 2028.

title: Medicare Advantage Improvement Act of 2026
